lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The résumé includes personal details that are conventionally left off.
items.because: Date of birth and nationality do not support your candidacy.

items.says: Education appears before the experience that demonstrates applied engineering and machine-learning work.
items.because: The order delays the evidence most relevant to your experience.

items.says: The 10-month gap between the B.S. and the next listed role is unexplained.
The 35% accuracy improvement has no stated baseline or definition.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what it was measured against or whether it is a relative increase or a percentage-point change.

items.says: The routing description uses dense, team-specific wording that makes the behavior hard to picture.
The reductions are buried after the GRPO method description.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the result only after the training details.

items.says: The harness bullet includes unnecessary process wording.
Assistant-only loss masking does not generally teach the model to reproduce tool outputs.
items.because: It typically excludes tool-role output tokens from the training loss.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking method is repeated without a distinct result.
items.because: The earlier bullet already describes the method, so this one adds no separate accomplishment.

items.says: “ML-extracted features” does not identify the feature-extraction or model step.
The strongest accomplishment in the internship entry is not the opening bullet.
Switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision alone does not generally reduce total GPU memory by 4×.
items.because: Mixed-precision fine-tuning may retain FP32 master weights and optimizer states, and the memory measure is unspecified.

items.says: The article in “the perception models” is unnecessary.
The load-test safeguard is a lengthy trailing detail.
The release-cycle bullet mixes past and present tense.
items.because: “Maintained” is past tense while “adds” is present tense in a completed role.

items.says: The three-day release-cycle duration has no comparison with the previous process.
items.because: The duration alone does not establish how much time was saved.

items.says: The backlog and dispatch outcome has no before-and-after measure.
items.because: A reader cannot gauge how often backlogs occurred or how much they delayed dispatch.

items.says: The opening bullet does not name the AI-first practices introduced.
The claimed downstream improvement is unspecified.
The strongest line in this project entry is not the opening one.
“Grew 100x” leaves the comparison implicit.
The reported removal of deadlocks and lost results lacks a before-and-after measure or confirming test result.
items.because: The 50-way condition does not show how the change was validated or how much it reduced failures.

items.says: The concurrency bullet uses team-specific shorthand that may be hard to scan.
The metrics integration bullet states what was added but not what it enabled.
items.because: A reader cannot tell why the integration mattered to the framework or its users.

items.says: The evaluator’s 0.89 Kendall correlation has no stated reference for comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what ranking or target the results were correlated against.

items.says: The test setup pushes the correlation result later in the bullet.
The project repeats a diagnostics-triage achievement that belongs under the internship, with a different reduction figure.
items.because: The 800+ signal triage and backlog reduction match the industrial-inspection result, where the reduction is 68%.

items.says: The backlog reduction has no starting point or timeframe.
items.because: “By two-thirds” does not show the starting backlog or when the reduction occurred.

items.says: The triage bullet does not explain how screening the signals informs triage.
items.because: The connection between the screening method and the backlog result is unclear.

items.says: The long method description after the result makes the bullet harder to scan.
items.because: The signal count and feature wording compete with the outcome rather than quickly explaining the core method.
